summary: LG Electronics India sells refrigerators, washing machines, air conditioners and televisions. It also supplies screens and other equipment to businesses.
description: The LG name on a fridge or TV in an Indian home usually refers to products marketed by LG Electronics India in this market. The company makes appliances locally and also buys certain finished goods and parts. It uses dealers, stores and online channels to reach households and business buyers.
money: It earns from appliances, screens and other goods it sells. It spends on materials, bought-in products, factory staff, shipping, promotion and after-sales support. A price cut can lift the number of appliances sold while leaving less money per sale.
customers: Households buy appliances and entertainment products. A retailer or distributor can be the company’s direct buyer and sell those products on. Business buyers also purchase display and cooling equipment.
drivers: Look at how many products customers buy, the price and features they choose, and how important parts and selling costs move through the year.

quick.title: What does it do?
quick.text: It makes and sells home appliances, air conditioners, televisions and related equipment.

quick.title: Who pays?
quick.text: Distributors, retailers, shoppers and business buyers pay for equipment.

quick.title: How does it earn?
quick.text: It earns mainly by selling products.

quick.title: What does it spend on?
quick.text: Parts and materials, finished goods bought from suppliers, manufacturing, promotion and service.

groups.title: Cold storage and laundry
groups.examples: Refrigerators, washing machines and washer dryers.
groups.explanation: These appliances cool food or handle laundry. Size and features help determine the price a household will pay.

groups.title: Room and building cooling
groups.examples: Window air conditioners, split systems and commercial cooling.
groups.explanation: A system moves heat away from a room or building. Larger buyers may need units fitted for different spaces.

groups.title: Home entertainment
groups.examples: Televisions, soundbars and other audio products.
groups.explanation: Shoppers buy screens and sound to watch broadcasts or streaming video at home.

groups.title: Screens for computers and businesses
groups.explanation: A monitor shows what a computer sends it. Business display equipment can show information or advertising in a public space.

basics.title: What are LG India’s two reported businesses?
basics.text: Its accounts group appliances and air cooling together and show home entertainment separately. The names refer to divisions of the Indian listed company.

basics.title: Why does the product mix matter?
basics.text: Mix means which products make up sales. More large refrigerators or higher priced TVs can change revenue and profit even when unit sales move little.

stepsTitle: From appliance production to a paid order

steps.title: Plan models and source parts
steps.text: Choose the range to sell and arrange supplies such as metal, plastics, motors and screens.

steps.title: Assemble and test products
steps.text: Factories put parts together and check finished units. The company also buys some finished goods.

steps.title: Move stock to buyers
steps.text: Send items to distributors and stores, or fulfil orders through direct and online channels.

steps.title: Record the sale and support the appliance
steps.text: Recognise revenue as control passes under the sale terms. Cash payment can follow later, and warranties and repairs have their own costs.

specifics.title: Cooling is especially sensitive to the weather
specifics.text: Dealers stock air conditioners ahead of summer. A short or mild hot season can leave more units to sell later.

specifics.title: Local production has a different cost structure
specifics.text: Manufacturing in India can shorten the supply route for selected products. Factory spending still has to be spread across the units actually produced.

specifics.title: This is the Indian listed company
specifics.text: Read LG Electronics India’s filings for this profile. Its figures cover the Indian company’s reported operations, including applicable export sales.

watch: Appliances and entertainment can grow at different speeds and have different costs.
Compare the two reported divisions’ sales and results before interest and tax. Check whether the larger division also retains a bigger share of its sales.
Did sales grow by selling more units or pricier ones?
The two paths can have different effects on profit and demand.
Look for category volumes, selling prices or comments on product mix. Check whether growth came from more units or higher priced models.
Are air conditioners selling through the channel?
Shipments to dealers and eventual purchases by households can happen at different times.
Compare cooling sales, weather commentary and stock levels after summer. See whether sales to dealers matched the demand they expected from shoppers.
Higher prices for metals, electronics or screens can reduce what a sale leaves behind.
Compare materials and product purchase costs with revenue. Read what the company says about pricing.
A factory can cost money even before enough products are sold to cover it.
Follow factory opening dates and compare future output and demand with spending plans. Look for when the company starts using each new line.
risks: Households can put off replacing expensive appliances.
Imported parts or products can cost more when the rupee weakens.
A newer display or feature can make existing inventory harder to sell at the original price.
Parts or shipping can be interrupted
A supply delay can reduce available products for weeks when demand is strongest.

helps.title: Many categories share the same sales network
helps.text: A buyer shopping for a washer may see other appliances through the same store or dealer.

helps.title: Some equipment is replaced after years of use
helps.text: Wear, repairs and changing needs create replacement demand.

helps.title: Installing and servicing equipment builds local reach
helps.text: Access to installation and support can matter when shoppers compare large appliances.

hurts.title: Discounts can reduce the amount earned per sale
hurts.text: Promotions help compete for an order but can narrow what the company keeps.

hurts.title: Consumer electronics require regular updates
hurts.text: Changing screens, features and energy efficiency can require fresh design and tooling.

hurts.title: Warranty obligations follow a sale
hurts.text: Support and repairs can add costs after the buyer has paid.

context: The company reported higher full-year sales and lower full-year profit after tax. Read the audited division results and company expenses to see why a sales increase need not lead to higher profit.
sources: Audited annual and segment results filed with NSE
LG India results announcement for the year to March 2026

financialNotes.title: Why the division profit differs from company profit
financialNotes.text: The two disclosed division results come before interest, head office and other unallocated costs, and tax. Read the company’s profit after tax separately.

financialCue: Compare division sales and segment results first. Use the reconciliation to see how company costs reduce the sum of those results.
